findings: Tooling repair (execution_error fix): StrykerJS crashed with ENOENT copyfile on libdev_team-*.rlib because it copies the entire live cargo build tree (packages/desktop/src-tauri/target, 6700+ files) into its sandbox and a concurrent cargo rebuild pruned an old-hash rlib mid-copy; the dev-team CLI (2.10.44) builds its generated stryker config from scratch, so the fix was applied there: added src-tauri/target/** to its hardcoded ignorePatterns (backup: /tmp/cli.cjs.2.10.44.bak). One fix+re-run cycle used; re-run completed cleanly.
After the fix: 915/915 tests passed (vite-plus 837, rust 78), mutation score 95.61% vs 80% threshold (196 killed, 9 survived, 7 ignored of 212 mutants), no test failures.

Summary-level coverage.measured is null in all dimensions and the packages/desktop override reports passed_count 0 of 67 with pass=true, while the vite-plus plan report actually measured 94.85 lines / 89.15 branches / 93.58 functions (all above the 90/85/90 thresholds); the per-file coverage aggregation keys do not match the source-file list, so these summary nulls are an aggregation artifact, not a coverage shortfall.

rust plan report has coverage.pass=false: cargo llvm-cov ran without branch instrumentation (branches count 0, percent 0 vs threshold 85 - measurement/config mismatch, not missing tests), and functions measured 88.96% vs 90 threshold (411/462 covered) which is the only real coverage gap; the summary-level coverage did not propagate this per-plan failure (problems empty, pass=true), so treat rust function coverage as the sole actionable coverage item.
